evidence: Cic. Rep. 2.12: novam interrēgnī ineundī ratiōnem (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: To find out by thinking: a plan, a method, a new thing. Lewis & Short: “frequent and classical”.

evidence: Cic. Dom. 1: multa dīvīnitus ā majōribus nostrīs inventa (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: Its plain sense is “find” (see find); “invent” is its figurative use. From it come inventor, inventōris m., an inventor (Aristaeus, quī olīvae dīcitur inventor, Cic. N.D. 3.45), and inventum, inventī n., an invention (Ov. Met. 1.521).

evidence: Ov. Met. 8.246: serrae reperit ūsum (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: Its plain sense is “find” (see find); “invent” is its figurative use, frequent after Augustus (Lewis & Short): Ovid’s Perdix serrae reperit ūsum, invented the saw. An inventor is also repertor.

phrases.latin: cum recentī fīcō salis vice cāseō vescī nūper excōgitātum est
phrases.english: eating cheese with a fresh fig instead of salt is a recent invention
